column1: # builds.tsv - what can be built, and out of what.
# This was apps.tsv, and it had thirty rows describing twenty builds. Seven of
# them were neutrinoloaders.js --testing under seven names -- neutrinocache,
# never a thing. It was "the loaders app, but appcache's copy of it", and that
# sentence was nowhere in the tree: the name said neither what it was built from
# nor who ran it, so answering either question meant reading the table.
# So the name of the artifact and the name of the build are two different jobs,
# and this file only does the second one. A row here says what a build IS. Which
# suite gets a copy, and what that copy is called, is suites.tsv's business --
# see the `build=` directive there. The artifact a suite runs is named after the
# suite, so `appcache` runs `test/out/appcache.cmd` and nothing has to be
# `builder` is mkapp or demoapp. Almost everything is mkapp.sh; the app on the
# download page is not, because test/build/demoapp.sh assembles pages/demo --
# the four files that ship -- with test/probe/demoprobe.js concatenated onto the
# app's own script, which no flag string could say.
# `source` is the .js under test/probe/ that mkapp.sh builds from. `-` where the
# `flags` is argv for the builder, `-` for none. A bare `--overlay <name>`
# resolves against test/probe/, the same way `source` does: the rooms are the
# runner's business, and a manifest carrying paths would be re-edited by every
# There is no output column any more. apps.tsv had one because "half the tree
# refers to that path by name"; nothing does now.
# A name says what the build is, not who asked for it. `-testing` and `-release`
# where both exist, because which one a lane runs is a fact about that lane and
# was invisible in the YAML until these tables existed: a testing build carries
# the trace channel, the macOS status file, the two windows environment
# overrides and Qt's --no-sandbox, and a release build does not carry them at
# Two builds that are a launcher part swapped rather than a flag. The overlay
# directory is the whole difference and it is named in the flags, so the reason
# the artifact differs is readable here rather than in a workflow.
